Operations that mutate state optimistically or trigger irreversible side effects before an async call resolves must be guarded against partial/failed outcomes. Sequence side effects so they only happen after success is confirmed, and on failure restore the prior known-good state rather than leaving the system in an inconsistent or misleading condition.

Concretely:
- Defer irreversible actions (detaching a session, discarding a draft, committing a UI toggle) until the dependent async call has actually succeeded. For example, detach a cloud session only after a local resume succeeds, not before attempting it, so a failed resume doesn't strand the user in a half-migrated state.
- When an optimistic UI update (e.g. switching a mode indicator) is followed by an async call that can reject, catch the rejection and explicitly roll the UI/state back to the previous value, resyncing from the authoritative source of truth (e.g. server/config state) rather than a locally captured snapshot:
```ts
const previousMode = session.uiMode;
session.toggleMode(); // optimistic
props.onModeChange(newMode).catch((error) => {
  session.setUiMode(previousMode); // roll back on failure
  showToast(error);
});
```
- When failure leaves the actual outcome ambiguous (e.g. it's unclear whether a request was delivered before the error occurred), do not assume success or failure and auto-recover data that might already be in flight; only restore/recover state you can prove was never dispatched.
- When displaying results after an error, avoid silently falling back to stale/cached success data (e.g. showing old model list) alongside the error message — make the error state explicit instead of implying the action still partially succeeded.

Applying this consistently prevents desynced state, data loss, and misleading UI after failures in async or multi-step operations.</description>
